subject: Crosswalk: contingency ledger & parallel acceptance paths
messages:
From: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone movement — need a short note for our steering

Sofia,

Quick note — our steering committee met this morning and they want a short explanation for the shift in the go-live window. They asked for: 1) top three technical risks that caused the drift, 2) a clear mitigation we can execute in the next 7 days, and 3) whether there are any parallel acceptance paths we can run to avoid a hard delay.

Can you send a one-page summary we can include in the pack? Procurement is also asking if any contract dates need to be updated (they'd like advance notice).

Thanks,
Ethan

--
Ethan Morris
Senior PM, Acme Cloud
ethan.morris@acme.com
+1 415 555 0123
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone movement — short summary and next steps

Ethan — thanks, we can absolutely provide that. High level here (I'll attach the one-pager and updated MAP):

Top 3 drivers of schedule variance
- Late SOC ingestion: our pre-prod environment received a delayed data dump; conversion and sanity checks slipped 3 business days.
- Eval gate regressions: two prompts in the payment flow showed quality regressions at longer context lengths; triggered a model variant rollback during test, which extended validation time.
- Procurement gating for the dedicated pool: cloud partner approval for additional capacity took longer than expected, limiting parallel test runs.

7-day mitigations (operational)
- Lock the current model variant and run a targeted fix-only eval set (we've scoped 1200 tokens worth of regression checks) — Marcus will lead.
- Run a small-scale parallel acceptance path: production-like traffic simulation on a sliced dataset (critical user flows only) — Laura to own.
- Temporary burst capacity from Cloud Partner to run parallel validation windows (request sent; partner on copy).

Parallel acceptance paths
- Acceptance A: full regression on gated environment (longer, gold standard).
- Acceptance B: sliced simulation on high-value flows + telemetry checks (fast, incremental acceptance).

I'll circulate the one-pager and updated MAP_v2.xlsx in 45 minutes. If steering wants a specific sentence for the pack, suggest: "Acme and Redwood agreed a short-term parallel acceptance path to validate critical flows while fixes are validated in the gated environment, reducing the risk of a hard go-live delay."

Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Accounts Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone movement — technical mitigation plan

Adding the technical detail for the one-pager and the 7-day play: 

- Root cause: ingestion schema mismatch created edge-case tokens that failed the tokenizer sanity checks; triggered fallback paths in the runtime and caused increased tail latency during eval.
- Immediate fix: a lightweight transformation step that normalizes the inbound payload (ETA: 36 hours) — will not change model weights.
- Validation plan: targeted eval set (see eval-gate-checklist.pdf) of 400 sample sessions + 50 full-length tokenized runs on the production-like slice. Expected validation window: 48–72 hours once data is normalized.
- Rollback guard: if any metric crosses the regression threshold (WER > 3% / latency p95 +40ms), we fallback to current pinned variant and expand parallel acceptance.

I've updated MAP_v2.xlsx with the task assignment and times. Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone movement — operations & procurement implications

Folks — quick procurement/ops notes for transparency:

- Procurement: if the formal go-live date shifts past 11/20 we need an amendment to the SOW for the reserved pool start date. Procurement, please confirm your preferred lead time.
- Ops: I recommend we run Acceptance B (sliced simulation) overnight for three consecutive nights; that gives us telemetry to decide on day 4. That keeps the Acceptance A window intact and reduces risk.
- Customer comms: Ethan, suggest we provide the steering panel with our proposed sentence from Sofia and the mitigation timeline (36 hours normalize -> 48–72 hours validate -> go/no-go decision).

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Cloud Partner <partner@cloudco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: MAP decision ledger — agreed parallel path, triggers, and escalation lane

Ethan / team — finalizing decisions from the last 48 hours and next steps for steering: 

Decisions made
- Parallel acceptance path B approved: three-night sliced simulation begins tonight (owner: Laura).
- Normalize ingestion step approved (owner: Marcus) — ETA 36 hours.
- Validation window: 48–72 hours post-normalization, then a go/no-go decision.
- Contract amendment trigger: if go-live slips beyond 2026-11-20, procurement will request an SOW amendment; procurement asked to be informed by 2026-11-18 EOD.

Escalation lane (if metrics fail)
- Day 1–3: Run Acceptance B and monitor p95 latency, error-rate, and quality regressions.
- If WER > 3% or latency delta exceeds +40ms at any point, automatically pause the canary and escalate to Execs: Laura -> VP CS -> Sales Leadership (cc'd list).

Artifacts attached to this mail: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated tasks), eval-gate-checklist.pdf (validation criteria), acceptance-parallel-paths.md (detailed ops runbook).

I'll prepare a 1-page summary for your steering pack and send it in the next hour. Thanks for the fast coordination — the approach should keep us on a low-risk path while preserving the acceptance gate.

Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Accounts Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
